div.head: Af 4.1
div.ab: Gif he hine selfne triowan wille, do þæt be cyninges wergelde.
Gif he hine sylfne treowan wylle, dó þæt be cyninges wergylde.
Gyf he hine sylfne treowsian wylle, do þæt be cyninges wergylde.
Si se uelit adlegiare, secundum regis weregildum hoc faciat.

Wenn er sich reinschwören will, thue er das mit [Eid so hoch wie] Königs Wergeld.
If he wishes to clear himself by oath, let him do so with [an oath as high as] the king’s wergeld.
If he wishes to clear himself [from such a charge], he shall do it by an oath equal to the king's wergeld.

Vgl. Gl Eidesschwere 4a; Wergeld 11. Der Königsverrats Angeklagte musste sich nach diesem System mit 36 Gemeinfreien reinigen oder, falls cynebot inbegriffen, mit 72
Cf. Gl Eidesschwere 4a; Wergeld 11. Under this system a man accused of treason against the king had to clear himself with 36 common freemen or, if cynebot was included, with 72

The value of the wergeld of the King of Wessex is never stated in the laws. In the fragment Be Myrcna Lage, cap. 2, the king’s (simple) wergeld is stated to be equal to the wergeld of six thegns, i.e., 30,000 sceattas or 120 pounds, while an equal amount, called cynebot, has to be paid to the leode (i.e. the men in the personal service of the king). As this is the sum stated to have been paid for the West Saxon prince Mul (see Sax. Chron. ann. 694), it would seem that the wergelds of the West Saxon and Mercian kings were originally identical. A different and somewhat larger sum is specified in the Northleoda Laga, cap. 1 (see Chadwick, Anglo-Saxon Institutions, p. 17 f.).
